title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics - Nature Energy
text:
AbstractBifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells offer a promising route to high area-normalized power output. Using ~1.55 eV perovskite absorbers reduces reliance on bromide, largely mitigating light-induced halide segregation and shifting the dominant stability challenge to the intrinsic photothermal resilience of bromide-lean absorbers. Here we identify perovskite lattice compliance, the ability of the crystal lattice to elastically accommodate stress, as a materials descriptor governing photothermal stability. Across the compositions studied, higher lattice compliance promotes photothermal stability by suppressing thermally induced microstrain accumulation, shifting deep-level defects towards shallower states and reducing band-edge energetic disorder. Guided by this absorber-level design principle, bifacial monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems achieved a power-generation density of 36.2 mW cm−2 under 0.20 albedo-equivalent illumination and retained 90% of their initial efficiency after over 1,000 h of ISOS-L-2 testing (1-sun at 65 °C). These results establish lattice compliance as a physically testable framework for designing stable perovskite absorbers.
